newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia industrial group sees slight recovery.
newsitem.headline: Colombia industrial group sees slight recovery.

text.p: Industrial production is showing signs of a return to positive growth after disastrous first quarter figures, but producer confidence is still at rockbottom, an independent industrial survey found.

In its monthly industrial poll, the influential National Association of Industrialists (ANDI) estimated industrial production posted negative growth of -1.2 percent in April, with a 0.4 percent drop in sales in the same month.
May figures, however, show production returning to positive growth, up 0.8 percent, and sales up 1.1 percent, the ANDI survey, issued Thursday, said.
Those results compare with a first quarter negative growth of -3.3 percent in industrial output and a 1.4 percent decline in sales, according to ANDI's calculations.

Official government figures showed first quarter industrial output, including coffee processing, down 5.4 percent compared with the same period last year. Excluding coffee processing, the January-March figure was down 6.94 percent compared with the first quarter of 1996, the government's National Statistics Department said.

Despite signs of a return to growth in May, ANDI said it was too early to speak of a full-blown recovery. "This upturn does not signify industrial recovery, especially when half the sectors surveyed are still seeing drops in production."

Those sectors still clearly in recession are leather goods, rubber products, transport equipment, non-ferrous metals, drinks and tobacco, ANDI said. Glassware, plastics, electrical machinery, iron and steel and paper products are all seeing an upturn, ANDI said.
Of those businesses surveyed 75 percent said the outlook for production was poor or regular. Only 21 percent of respondents said they saw the situation picking up in the coming months.
